text:
mira: Heads up — customer AcmePay opened a ticket: they were billed for 720 reserved GPU hours for March but their usage dashboard shows ~320 reserved hours and heavy token usage only on two days. Billing says no credits applied. Can someone triage?

samir: Ack. Ticket #C-3248? I pulled invoices, the reserved commit line is 720h. Dashboard (internal) shows reserved_pool.hours_consumed = 320. :confused:

lee: Adding context — their Dedicated pool has burst enabled (auto-burst to shared) and we saw 2 big burst days (Mar 10 & Mar 22) where token throughput spiked. Could billing have attributed burst time differently?

billing-bot: Invoice C-3248: reserved_capacity_charge=720h * $X/hr. SLA_credit_policy: credits applied only when measured uptime < SLA threshold. No auto-credit for over-commit or mismatch between token_metering and reserved_hours.

mira: Customer insists reserved hours should match what the reserved pool metering shows, not invoice. They claim we double-counted burst hours as reserved. Repro steps requested.

samir: Quick repro I ran against metering service:
```
GET /v1/metering/reserved_hours?pool=acmepay-main&start=2025-03-01&end=2025-03-31
Response: {"reserved_hours_billed":720, "reserved_hours_used":320, "burst_hours":400}
```
Seems like backend is returning billed=reserved_hours_commit (contract) separate from used. But burst_hours shows 400, summing to 720. Is that correct accounting?

lee: That sounds like we're summing reserved_used + burst_used then billing reserved_commit separately. We should bill reserved_commit regardless of burst, but the invoice shouldn't double-charge for burst if burst is charged differently — need to confirm pricing rules for burst in their contract.

oncall-ops: I checked routing logs for those spike days — a portion of the spike routed to shared pool due to autoscaling mis-attachment. Trace snippets:
```
2025-03-10T14:02:05Z route=dedicated_pool->shared_pool reason=burst_below_threshold
2025-03-22T09:13:41Z route=dedicated_pool->shared_pool reason=burst_exhausted
```
So some tokens were served from shared capacity. That should generate seperate usage lines (burst usage).

anna: Internal pricing note: reserved commit is charged as a fixed line item (customer contract). Bursts are charged on top unless they consume the reserved pool first. For customers who enable auto-burst, billing shows: reserved_commit_charge + burst_overage_charge. But customer says they only saw token consumption matching reserved hours and no separate burst invoice line.

mira: Hmm. Customer's dashboard doesn't surface burst_overage line because UI aggregates under "Compute usage" and hides separate burst lines unless you click export. They missed it. Need to confirm invoice lines and whether credits apply for misrouting.

samir: I exported their raw usage CSV and found columns: date, pool, mode, gpu_hours, token_count. Snip:
```
2025-03-10,acmepay-main,dedicated,8,12_000_000
2025-03-10,acmepay-main,burst_shared,16,20_000_000
```
That matches the 24h total for the day but invoice shows only reserved_commit + no explicit burst line. Possible bug in invoice generator where burst_shared entries with pool=acmepay-main are folded into reserved_commit aggregate.

lee: If invoice generator aggregates by pool and ignores mode, that would explain missing burst_overage lines and apparent double billing (customer thinks we billed 720h for single commit but also charged tokens). We should check billing report grouping logic.

billing-bot: Billing pipeline note: aggregator_v2 groups by (customer_id, pool_name) and sums gpu_hours. mode field historically ignored — fallback when older schema. A migration in 2025-02 added mode, but aggregator flag 'respect_mode' might be off for some accounts.

mira: Action items: (1) samir/lee — run a targeted aggregation for AcmePay to compute per-mode charges and compare to invoice; (2) billing team (anna) verify if 'respect_mode' flag was enabled for their account; (3) oncall-ops check if misrouting created any SLA credit eligibility.

anna: Will check the account flags and invoice generation logs. If we find invoice mis-aggregation we'll draft a credit and reissue. ETA EOD.

samir: I ran the per-mode aggregation query:
```
SELECT mode, SUM(gpu_hours) FROM usage_raw WHERE account='acmepay' AND month='2025-03' GROUP BY mode;
-- results: dedicated:320, burst_shared:400
```
Charge calc if correct: reserved_commit_charge = 720h (contract) but burst_overage_charge should apply only for burst_shared 400h if contract allows. Our invoice shows only 720h line, no burst line. So bug in invoice generator likely suppressed burst charges (customer actually got billed reserved_commit only) — customer claim was opposite; they thought we double-charged. Need to reconcile with transaction-level ledger.

mira: Good catch. Let's pull ledger entries for March (transaction-level). If invoice generator suppressed burst lines, ledger will show whether we charged burst_overage. If ledger has no burst charge then customer billing amount may be correct and their dashboard confusion caused the complaint. If ledger DOES have burst charges + 720 line then it's a real double-charge.

anna: Pulling ledger now. Will post findings.

billing-bot: Ledger query in progress...

(30m later)

anna: Update — ledger shows two separate charges: reserved_commit 720h and burst_overage 0h (zero). Invoice line for burst was suppressed due to zero-valued entries being filtered out. The invoice amount equals reserved_commit only. So customer was billed only for commit. However UI export included burst_shared usage rows even if overage price was zero due to a promotion applied earlier — that caused them to think we billed both.

mira: TL;DR: No double-charge. Root causes: (A) promotional override made burst price zero for March, (B) dashboard export shows mode-level usage (includes burst_shared) but invoice showed only billed lines, (C) invoice generator suppressed zero-value lines which confused customers.

lee: Proposed fix: (1) billing UI — show "Invoiceed charges (including zeroed promotions)" toggle or explicit line for zero-priced bursts with annotation, (2) aggregator flag cleanup to respect mode consistently, (3) ops to review routing misattachments but no credit needed since SLA unaffected.

samir: I'll prepare a short internal note and the query outputs to attach to the customer reply.

mira: I'll respond to AcmePay with findings and a clear export showing "usage rows (token/gpu)" vs "charged invoice lines" and confirm no double-billing. cc @anna for follow-up if they still dispute. :thumbsup:
